chapter_title: Learning Experience Design and Software Technology
title: LXD Optimizer Critical Use
description: AIL 606 textbook section connecting lxd optimizer critical use to storyboard frame sequence with narration, signaling, and reader-action notes, reader notes, support moments, and revision evidence.
learning_objectives: Classify an optimizer suggestion as goal-aligned, goal-neutral, or goal-opposed by reading its mechanism before its predicted-gain magnitude.
Explain why engagement proxies (completion, time-on-page, efficiency) cannot on their own certify that learning occurred, using Goodhart's law.
Defend an accessibility provision against an efficiency edit on UDL learner-variability grounds the usage metric cannot see.
Produce a triaged optimizer report with a per-row verdict and mechanism, at least one reasoned rejection, and a before-after transfer check on the accepted edit.
